text: Platinum Trading APP — 12/26/21, 10:00 PM Sunday, December 26, 2021 at 10:00 PM DAY TRADING PART 5 SUPPORT AND RESISTANCE Support and Resistance are two of the most important things to know in trading. Almost every trade you take will have reasoning based off of one of these areas. What is a Support and Resistance? Support and resistance area price range that a stock price tends to stay in. If a breakout occurs through the resistance, a price can go higher and old resistance can act as a new support. Does a Support/Resistance always work? A Support or Resistance does not work every time, just as every other trading strategy isn't 100% accurate either. This is why we must use stop losses and price targets to protect our capital. The price may never hit the resistance level or may break below support, so that is one thing to keep in mind, so lock in profits when possible! Platinum Trading © DAY TRADING PART 6 TRENDLINES You can have a support and resistance level that is different from the regular horizontal one. You can have diagonal ones as well. Here is a quick overview of some common patterns with trendlines. Platinum Trading © DAY TRADING PART 7 HOW TO TRADE BREAKOUTS A breakout is a break over a previous resistance level when playing the long side. A breakout can push a stock up higher but not always so it is something to be careful of. Here are a few common breakout patterns you can use as a reference for future trades. Bull Flag Pattern Entry will be either at the bottom red line or when it breaks out of the triangle. You will want to wait for the confirmation of the candles holding above the resistance level before taking an entry. Your stop loss will be at the bottom of the support or below the previous resistance level. Horizontal Support and Resistance Entry will be at the bottom of the pattern with the confirmation of the candles bouncing on the on the support or on a breakout of the resistance level at the top. Stop Loss will be below the support or below the resistance level if you are trading the breakout. Ascending Triangle Pattern Entry will be at the bottom of the pattern with the confirmation of the candles bouncing on trendline or breaking out of upper trendline . Stop loss when there is a break below the support level or resistance if playing the top level Platinum Trading © DAY TRADING PART 8 VWAP The Volume Weighted Average Price is my favorite indicator to use for day trading. It is usually represented as a thin line which closely follows the stock candles. The best way to use this indicator is to play breaks and dips. To play a break, buy right as the candles break above the VWAP line. To buy dips, try to enter the stock right when it is touching the VWAP but it doesn't break below it. You may also use the upper and lower bands of the VWAP using this method. The bottom VWAP band can act as support. The middle can act as resistance. And when price moves above the middle swap, the middle VWAP can act as a support and the top VWAP can act as a new resistance. Always remember old resistance becomes new support, and old support can become new resistance as well! Platinum Trading ©

text: PT | Nitro Trades [PLAT], Server Tag: PLAT PLAT CEO — 11/26/23, 3:59 PM Sunday, November 26, 2023 at 3:59 PM @everyone Here is my personal trading plan that I use for my own trades Feel free to use it and tweak it to your own strategy TRADING PLAN 1. Has to be a good fair value gap, supply/demand, orderblock, or Opening Range Breakout 2. Price has to react to the zone. Basically showing a wick or some kind of bounce from the zone. If there is no reaction to the zone, then you do not enter. 3. Never enter with more than 5-10% of your portfolio on a single trade (10% being a very high confidence setup) 4. Stop Loss must be tight, if it hits even instantly you sell no matter what. NEVER EVER Let a trade go past 20-25% loss (MOST IMPORTANT) 5. Try to scale out of positions. Once you take your first scale out of the position, raise your stop loss to right around breakeven. Keep raising your stop loss if you don't trade with targets, until the SL hits 6. Always exit at price target and don't look back even if it runs 500% after you exit. You can hold one contract as a runner if you see more range, but always exit majority at targets. 7. If you are not fully confident on a trade, don't enter. However, if you do want to try the trade still that is what we call a LOTTO. Only 1% of your portfolio for sizing and no adding size to it 8. Follow this plan every trading day very strictly and watch your trading improve. The only time you will lose is if you break the rules of the plan

text: Platinum Trading APP — 10/6/22, 12:58 AM Thursday, October 6, 2022 at 12:58 AM Introduction Stocks are used to buy a "part" of a company. When entering a stock, you are expecting the stock price to go up because it is a good company. For example, If I am buying a share of Netflix (NFLX) I think it will go up in the future so I can sell it for more than I bought it at. If you bought those shares of Netflix at $100 and they went to $500 a share, you made $400 a share profit. Other than buying to sell the shares in the future, you may as a means of receiving "dividends". Dividends are percentages of revenue from a company that you receive based on the amount of shares you own. So in basic terms, you buy a share in a company you believe has potential to grow so you can sell those shares for a profit later on. Terminology PT - Price Target SL - Stop Loss Scalp - also known as a daytrade. Quickly getting in and out of a stock. Short Swing - buying a stock to hold throughout the day typically an overnight position expecting it to increase over time Long Swing - Buying a stock at a good entry and holding for weeks or months Short Squeeze - A short squeeze occurs when a stock or other asset jumps sharply higher, forcing traders who had bet that its price would fall to buy it in order to forestall even greater losses. Their scramble to buy only adds to the upward pressure on the stock's price. Limit buy - buying at that exact share price and not any higher Market buy/sell order - buying/selling in the open market (don’t do it with penny stocks we trade) use limit buy/sell to get the best spread Reverse split - Company doesn’t meet requirements to stay listed as is on the exchange Tutes - institutions, big brokerages aka hedge funds. “Big money” that can have large impact on a stock HOD - High of the Day Finding Stocks to Buy The hardest part of trading/investing for most people, is finding what stocks to buy. The best way to get some experience in the market is to buy shares of some big companies. I have listed some of them below BIG NAME STOCKS LIST AMZN - Amazon TSLA - Tesla NFLX - Netflix TWTR - Twitter AAPL - Apple SPY - Spyder ETF FB - Facebook A quick pro tip for buying any of these stocks, is to average into positions if longer term rather than fully enter at once. Paper Trading An amazing way to practice stock trading/investing with zero risk is paper trading. Paper trading allows you to buy and sell stocks with fake money, which is amazing for those who are looking to learn with risking any money. You can use the paper trading system in Webull to practice. Stock Market Tips Before entering a trade, make sure of a few things : Have a stop loss and price target set - Make sure to have a point in where you will sell for minimal losses. Make sure to also not get greedy and take profits at some point. Make sure to do adequate research before entering - Never blindly enter a trade without adequate research. Know what you are trading. Always buy the dips, sell the rips - Whenever everyone is panicking because of a price drop, that's when you buy. Buy low, sell high. Do not trade with emotions!!! - This one is important. DO NOT buy a stock at all time high prices because of FOMO , (Fear of missing out). This is how you lose money in the market. Wait for dips and load up. Don't trade with money you can't afford to lose - Never use your rent money to trade as the market is unpredictable. You could make 100k in one day or lose 20k in one day. You never know so trade with money you can afford to lose! Good Videos for Learning Introduction to market - https://youtu.be/dFAiChOmoGI Support and Resistance - https://youtu.be/SgXOw_wOaBw Trading Breakouts - https://youtu.be/yGfAUia6b_g Day Trading - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I4yiHiM8OgI Swing Trading - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwVSUnb7cM8

author: Platinum Trading
text: Platinum Trading APP — 10/6/22, 1:31 AM Thursday, October 6, 2022 at 1:31 AM Options Basics An options contract gives you the ability to buy 100 shares of a stock at a set price. Options are much riskier than stocks, but generate higher profit. Options contracts follow the moves of the stock you are playing. For example, every .10 cents a stock moves, the contract moves up $1 (or .1 each contract). Options also have an expiration date and the contract value goes down everyday as you head towards that expiration. Options require a lot of practice and skill, so play with small amounts or paper trade first. Options Terminology • Call - Bullish position • Put - Bearish position • Weekly Call/Weekly Put - Expiration at end of week Friday • DT - Day trade • Swing- Position held overnight or longer • Leap- Long held contract up to many months to years • Scalp- extremely fast paced entry and exit, within minutes • Open interest- how many contracts are being held in total. • Volume- Contracts traded in the day’s trading session. • IV- Implied Volatility • BTO- Buy to Open • STC- Sell to Close • STO- Sell to Open • BTC- Buy to Close • Scale Out- Sell some positions for profit, slowly let remaining ride up • All out/Exit- Close all positions • Lotto- Extremely high-risk contract. High risk, high reward Options Greeks Delta - Delta is one of the two main greeks of options. The Delta of a contract is how much the price of the contract (or premium of the contract) will change compared to the underlying asset which in this case is the stock. For every $1 the stock moves, your contract moves the corresponding delta value of the contract. If you bought a contract at a premium of 3.00 with a delta of .50 when the stock was $75 per share, the contract will gain .50 of value for every $1 the stock goes up. So in this example if the stock moved up to $76 per share your contract would be worth 3.50. The higher the delta on your contract the more volatile that contract's premium will be. The lower your delta the less expected your contract is to be in the money (ITM) before it expires. If your delta is only 0.15 it means there’s currently only ~15% chance of your contract being in the money (ITM) before expiration. The Delta on a contract goes up and down based on the stocks price, if the stock gets closer to the strike price the delta will go up and if the stock goes further from the stocks price the delta goes down. Theta - Theta is the other main greek that you’ll want to know to be able to trade options. Theta is time decay or how much value your contract's premium will lose everyday. If your contract’s premium is 1.50 and the theta is -0.20 then your contract will lose 0.20 of value the next day simply from time decay. When looking to swing a contract or buy leaps the extremely ideal situation is finding a contract whose theta is 5% or less than the contract’s premium. A good example of this would be buying a contract whose premium is 1.00 with a theta of 0.05 or less. This means your premium only loses 0.05 or less per day. Those two are the two main greeks that will affect your options contract but they aren’t the only ones. text: Platinum Trading APP — 10/6/22, 12:58 AM Thursday, October 6, 2022 at 12:58 AM Introduction Stocks are used to buy a "part" of a company. When entering a stock, you are expecting the stock price to go up because it is a good company. For example, If I am buying a share of Netflix (NFLX) I think it will go up in the future so I can sell it for more than I bought it at. If you bought those shares of Netflix at $100 and they went to $500 a share, you made $400 a share profit. Other than buying to sell the shares in the future, you may as a means of receiving "dividends". Dividends are percentages of revenue from a company that you receive based on the amount of shares you own. So in basic terms, you buy a share in a company you believe has potential to grow so you can sell those shares for a profit later on. Terminology PT - Price Target SL - Stop Loss Scalp - also known as a daytrade. Quickly getting in and out of a stock. Short Swing - buying a stock to hold throughout the day typically an overnight position expecting it to increase over time Long Swing - Buying a stock at a good entry and holding for weeks or months Short Squeeze - A short squeeze occurs when a stock or other asset jumps sharply higher, forcing traders who had bet that its price would fall to buy it in order to forestall even greater losses. Their scramble to buy only adds to the upward pressure on the stock's price. Limit buy - buying at that exact share price and not any higher Market buy/sell order - buying/selling in the open market (don’t do it with penny stocks we trade) use limit buy/sell to get the best spread Reverse split - Company doesn’t meet requirements to stay listed as is on the exchange Tutes - institutions, big brokerages aka hedge funds. “Big money” that can have large impact on a stock HOD - High of the Day Finding Stocks to Buy The hardest part of trading/investing for most people, is finding what stocks to buy. The best way to get some experience in the market is to buy shares of some big companies. I have listed some of them below BIG NAME STOCKS LIST AMZN - Amazon TSLA - Tesla NFLX - Netflix TWTR - Twitter AAPL - Apple SPY - Spyder ETF FB - Facebook A quick pro tip for buying any of these stocks, is to average into positions if longer term rather than fully enter at once. Paper Trading An amazing way to practice stock trading/investing with zero risk is paper trading. Paper trading allows you to buy and sell stocks with fake money, which is amazing for those who are looking to learn with risking any money. You can use the paper trading system in Webull to practice. Stock Market Tips Before entering a trade, make sure of a few things : Have a stop loss and price target set - Make sure to have a point in where you will sell for minimal losses. Make sure to also not get greedy and take profits at some point. Make sure to do adequate research before entering - Never blindly enter a trade without adequate research. Know what you are trading. Always buy the dips, sell the rips - Whenever everyone is panicking because of a price drop, that's when you buy. Buy low, sell high. Do not trade with emotions!!! - This one is important. DO NOT buy a stock at all time high prices because of FOMO , (Fear of missing out). This is how you lose money in the market. Wait for dips and load up. Don't trade with money you can't afford to lose - Never use your rent money to trade as the market is unpredictable. You could make 100k in one day or lose 20k in one day. You never know so trade with money you can afford to lose! text: INTRODUCTION TO DAY TRADING What Is Day Trading? Day trading is buying and selling a stock in the same day. This is more risky than investing and swing trading as stocks are more volatile in day trading and can result in faster drops and pops. How Do I Day Trade? In order to day trade, you will need a cash account or a margin account with over $25,000. Don't start day trading until you have mastered a strategy for it. You may practice your strategies for day trading using a paper trading account until you get the full hang of it. Should I Start As A Day Trader? It is not a great idea to get into day trading before you understand swing trading and investing very well. Day Trading looks very appealing but without a proper idea of how it works, you can potentially blow up your account. Platinum Trading © Platinum Trading © DAY TRADING PART 1 HOW TO FIND STOCKS TO DAY TRADE 1. Find a website where you can view the top gainers for the trading day. You may use this webull top gainer scanner which is completely free. https://app.webull.com/market/region/6 2. Look for stocks under $20-25 that are up over 10-20% on the day. Keep a small watchlist of up to 6 stocks that are setting up nicely from this list and watch them for potential entries. 3. Keep the scanners up in case there are new stocks that run later on in the day. You don't have to stick with the same stocks throughout the entire day as stocks move every second. Platinum Trading © Platinum Trading © DAY TRADING PART 2 STOP LOSSES AND PRICE TARGETS Before entering any trade, you should have your Stop Losses and Price Targets already set. You can find these levels using support/resistance levels or based off of % W/L. Below are a few examples of ways to use Stop Losses and Price Targets : Level Based Price Target The nearest resistance level to your entry. For example, I buy a stock @ $5.30 a share and the next nearest resistance level is $5.60. I will place a sell order a little bit below that level at around $5.55-.58. If it hits this level, look to sell a few shares and not hold given profits into a loss. Level Based Stop Loss The nearest level below a support to cut losses. For example, I buy a stock at $5.40 and the support is at $5.30. I will look to put my stop loss at around $5.25-5.28 to stop further losses. % Based Price target Taking profits based off the amount of profit you are in. For example, before I entered the trade I had my price targets set at 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, and so on. So once my stock makes 5% profit I will look to sell some shares and keep going until I am happy with entirely selling. % Based Stop Loss Stopping Losses based off the amount of loss you are in. For example, before I entered the trade my stop loss was at 5%. Once my position is @ -5%, I will sell and not look back. You can also raise your stop loss into profit as the trade keeps rising, this way you can guarantee profits without letting a green trade turn red. VERY IMPORTANT TO RESPECT YOUR LEVELS - DO NOT HOLD A STOCK PAST STOP LOSS UNLESS YOU ARE 100% CONFIDENT IT WILL GO UP. IF IT HITS STOP LOSS SELL AND MOVE ON TO THE NEXT TRADE. Platinum Trading © Platinum Trading © DAY TRADING PART 3 HOW TO USE DIFFERENT TYPES OF ORDERS What is an order? An order is what you use to buy and sell a stock. For example, clicking "buy" on your broker is a way to place an order but it isn't the most efficient way. Here are some of the best ways to place orders for trades : • Market Order -Buy or sell @ Market Price • Limit Order - Buy or sell @ a price you set • Stop Loss - You can set a stop loss order if a stock falls below a certain price to automatically sell your shares(This then becomes a market order) • Stop limit - A limit you set that your stock will sell at a specific price. • Trailing stop loss % - Moving Stop Loss as stock moves up. Market order version • Trailing stop limit% - Moving Stop Loss as stock moves up. Limit order version Platinum Trading © Platinum Trading © DAY TRADING PART 4 GOING LONG VS SHORT In the stock market, there are multiple ways to trade a stock other than playing the "long" side or bet on it going up. You may also "short" a stock or bet on it going down. Here is a quick overview of how both types of traders trade. • Taking a long position on a stock is placing your money on a stock knowing that the price should go up based on your technical analysis of the stock. • Taking a short position on a stock are borrowed shares from your broker selling at a high price and later on bought at a lower price, And whatever profit you make you pocket the difference. You can only short with a margin account. Both methods of trading can yield great results and there is no need to only stick to one or the other. Try out both and see what works best for you. However, I do recommend you go into shorting after trying "longing" first as there are additional things in shorting that are more complicated that wouldn't be on trading with the long side. text: Ace♠ — 5/24/22, 6:08 PM Tuesday, May 24, 2022 at 6:08 PM Phantom/Error Candles Good evening guys, I thought I’d take the time and explain a quick thing to you all! Many of you, well most of you actually, at some point have sent a photo in After hours or Pre market of candles with huge wicks wondering why that happened, well here’s the explanation: Phantom wicks or error wicks, whatever you want to call them, are usually system errors by the broker. These candle shouldn’t be graphed but are sometimes (only in AH and PM). These candles are usually caused by big exchanges between brokers which is why you only see this happen to bigger cap stocks that have more shares/market cap. These could also be huge dark pool orders at times, although that hasn’t been proven to be 100% true. If you ever see one of these candles, DONT be alarmed, it will N E V E R trigger your Stop Loss if you do have one in place. Example of a phantom candle/wick is shown below @Premium Member

author: Option Sniper
text: Option Sniper APP — 8/20/26, 4:24 PM Thursday, August 20, 2026 at 4:24 PM @Option Sniper (edited) Thursday, August 20, 2026 at 4:27 PM Option Sniper v1.14 is live — your prices now ride Schwab's streaming feed. Grab it from the download page: https://www.tradingdecoded.com/option-sniper Why this release exists: on the morning of the 20th, Schwab's regular quote service fell apart for about five minutes — three to thirteen seconds per price check. Entries crawled, exits lagged, and a few of you got hurt. People running on Schwab's streaming feed never saw it. So now the app runs on that feed too. What changed: Streaming prices while you're in a trade. The moment you're in, Schwab pushes the bid to the app as it changes instead of the app asking once a second. Your stop and target react faster. The once-a-second check doesn't go away — it runs every five seconds as a truth check on the stream, and if the stream ever goes quiet or disagrees, the app drops straight back to full-speed polling on its own. You don't touch anything. A banner when Schwab is slow. If your broker's quote service bogs down, the app says so — with how far behind the quotes are — and clears it when things recover. It never blocks a button. A LIVE / POLL tag in the exit strip so you can see which feed is carrying your price at any moment. Both protect you; it's just telling you which. If you run your own program on Schwab's streaming connection: Schwab allows one per account and the app will not fight you for it. Flip off Use streaming prices in Settings and the app never touches it. As always, install it before the open or after the close. The installer has to close the app, and you don't want that happening while you're holding a position. 3 Add Reaction

Also, just to fill you in — I run a copy-trading bot that reads typed Discord signals and executes them in under a second. The real bottleneck is the typing: by the time a trader types his alert, the fill is already seconds old, and you know every second counts. So I built the fix, and I think you'd love it: a Fill Announcer. A small read-only script that watches your broker account and auto-posts every fill to your channel the moment it happens: ENTRY TSLA 345P 8/28 @ 4.24 x1 TSLA 345P +20% (4.24 → 5.10) EXIT TSLA 345P @ 5.10 x1 (+20%) Your members get your real entries, real average, and real exits to the second — zero typing, and it posts progress milestones (+10/+20/+30%…) and stop-outs by itself. Connecting is genuinely 5 minutes: Channel Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → copy the URL Paste that URL + your broker's read-only API key into one settings file Run the script. Done — it can't place, cancel, or touch anything, it only reads fills.

author: Ace♠
text: Ace♠ — 5/24/22, 6:08 PM Tuesday, May 24, 2022 at 6:08 PM Phantom/Error Candles Good evening guys, I thought I’d take the time and explain a quick thing to you all! Many of you, well most of you actually, at some point have sent a photo in After hours or Pre market of candles with huge wicks wondering why that happened, well here’s the explanation: Phantom wicks or error wicks, whatever you want to call them, are usually system errors by the broker. These candle shouldn’t be graphed but are sometimes (only in AH and PM). These candles are usually caused by big exchanges between brokers which is why you only see this happen to bigger cap stocks that have more shares/market cap. These could also be huge dark pool orders at times, although that hasn’t been proven to be 100% true. If you ever see one of these candles, DONT be alarmed, it will N E V E R trigger your Stop Loss if you do have one in place. Example of a phantom candle/wick is shown below @Premium Member 1 1 Add Reaction

text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. BTO = Buy To Open STC = Sell To Close STO = Sell To Open BTC = Buy To Close C = Call P = Put ITM = In The Money ATM = At The Money OTM = Outside The Money SL = Stop Loss PT = Price Target HOD = High of Day LOD = Low of Day ATH = All Time High ER = Earnings Report EOD = End of Day B/O = Breakout Pre / PM = Premarket AH = After Hours FOMO = Fear of Missing Out R/R = Risk Reward DD = Due Diligence PDT = Pattern Day Trader ETF = Exchange Traded Funds TA = Technical Analysis FA = Fundamental Analysis IPO = Initial Public Offering GTC = Good Til’ Canceled (order) GTD = Good Til’ Date (order) MM = Market Maker YOLO = You Only Live Once EMA = exponential moving average. RSI = relative strength index. VWAP = volume weighted average price. SS = short sell. Momo = momentum. Welcome to VIP Alerts ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 is option signals from our analysts. Read the format guide above before your first one. ⁠🛸spread-alerts is option spread signals from our analysts. ⁠🎰lotto-alerts is lottery ticket plays. Very high risk. These can go to zero. ⁠⚠stock-alerts-⚠ is where we alert our stock picks. ⁠💪member-alerts💪 Post your own trades or see what other members are trading. These are member posts, not analyst calls. ⁠trade-log is an automatic log of every ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 position, open and closed, posted by @TradesTracker ⁠🔵options-watchlist is posted every morning before the open. Names we are watching and the triggers to watch. View the pinned message in ⁠🔵options-watchlist for more info. Trading School at the bottom of the server covers the fundamentals. text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. BTO = Buy To Open STC = Sell To Close STO = Sell To Open BTC = Buy To Close C = Call P = Put ITM = In The Money ATM = At The Money OTM = Outside The Money SL = Stop Loss PT = Price Target HOD = High of Day LOD = Low of Day ATH = All Time High ER = Earnings Report EOD = End of Day B/O = Breakout Pre / PM = Premarket AH = After Hours FOMO = Fear of Missing Out R/R = Risk Reward DD = Due Diligence PDT = Pattern Day Trader ETF = Exchange Traded Funds TA = Technical Analysis FA = Fundamental Analysis IPO = Initial Public Offering GTC = Good Til’ Canceled (order) GTD = Good Til’ Date (order) MM = Market Maker YOLO = You Only Live Once EMA = exponential moving average. RSI = relative strength index. VWAP = volume weighted average price. SS = short sell. Momo = momentum. Welcome to VIP Alerts ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 is option signals from our analysts. Read the format guide above before your first one. ⁠🛸spread-alerts is option spread signals from our analysts. ⁠🎰lotto-alerts is lottery ticket plays. Very high risk. author: TradingTheTrend
text: [ 10:10 PM ] Saturday, January 23, 2021 at 10:10 PM As traders we know we are going to lose some trades. We will never be 100% perfect. You have to minimize your losses, and maximize your gains. If you always are selling too early, you are missing out on a big portion of your winning % You have to take advantage of the big wins, or your losses will overtake your gains. This is one of the reasons I suggest to always buy at least 2 contracts so you can leave a runner. Options trading is very risky. Never trade with what you cannot afford to lose. If you are new to options, I suggest you start out by paper trading. When you think you are ready, put in a small amount to play around with. You WILL blow accounts, and you WILL lose. It's part of it, and a part of the learning process. It is one of those things where you really just have to learn the hard way. Take every loss you have and go back over, figure out where you went wrong. What signs did you miss? What did the chart tell you? Did you use a stop loss? What can you do to avoid this in the future? Imprint the errors you made into your brain and never make them again. Weeklies are very risky and should only represent a small % of your portfolio. I cannot stress this enough. Yes, weeklies are fun and exciting, and can yield insane results.. But they are the most risky, unforgiving type of trade you can take. Veteran traders know better than to put big capital on risky trades. DIVERSIFY, SHARES, SPREADS, LEAPS>MONTHLIES>WEEKLIES TIME=MONEY I take profits from risky trades and add them to my long term positions. Sleep better, risk less, give yourself a chance to come back if the market falls. You can still yield insane results from long term trades. As long as you are being safe, following your plan, and using proper ⁠hedging techniques, you will have nothing to worry about in any market environment. (edited) Saturday, April 17, 2021 at 4:22 PM

author: beendoubleyou
text: beendoubleyou — 7/13/22, 5:25 PM Wednesday, July 13, 2022 at 5:25 PM Ok, so ghetto closing spreads to avoid using a day trade. Before we get into strikes, expiration, etc lets talk big picture. When you do a ghetto spread single leg options, the concept is easy. You buy a call or put at one strike for a certain price. Then you sell a different strike at a HIGHER premium to lock in profit. For example if I bought a call for $1.05 then I would be looking to sell a call at a higher strike for more than $1.05 and therefore locking in my profit. With spreads the concept is the same. Typically though we enter the credit spread first, so the concept is just backwards. Lets say I open a credit spread that has a $5 width, that means I'm using $500 in collateral. If I receive $0.40 for that position that means my max loss is $500 - $40 = $460 So really I'm risking $460 to make $40. Keep in mind that risk. I want my $500 back in collateral, that's the goal. I already received the $40 credit and I can do whatever I want with that money. I can never lose it. That's mine to keep, buy coffee, buy a new Xbox game, whatever. It's the $500 that I'm worried about now. I want that back. So lets say the market is moving in my favor and that $40 credit is pretty much maxed out, but I'm worried that things might change. So I want to ghetto close it. I do that by opening up a DEBIT position. A debit position is just the opposite of the credit position. So if open up a debit spread that is also $5 in width that means the max the position will ever be worth is $500 minus the cost of entering. So if I open up a debit spread and it COSTS me $0.10 to do so, that means my max profit is $500 - $10 = $490 If the ticker starts to move in that direction, then my max profit if those close in the money will be $490

author: beendoubleyou
text: beendoubleyou — 12/16/21, 5:05 PM Thursday, December 16, 2021 at 5:05 PM Ok, let's talk about these leaps I got today. Obviously the plan is have them go up, but I also plan on collecting some additional premium by making them a diagonal spread for the next year. You do this by selling calls at a higher strike with a closer expiration. Just like selling covered calls. You don't actually have the 100 shares, but the long call acts like 100 shares so you're allowed to sell calls against it. I know what you're thinking, "but those strikes are way out of the money, you can't sell calls against it!" Yes and no. Take NVDA for example, $400 strike, but it's for over a year out. Sure, I won't be able to collect anything trying to sell the Dec 17th $405 strike...because that's tomorrow and NVDA isn't jumping over $100 tomorrow, even with it being quad witching. But.....I can sell the Dec 31st $405 strike and collect about $20 for it. I doubt NVDA reaches $405 by Dec 31st so that seems like an easy $20 Now imagine collecting that $20 per contract every few weeks for the next year. That's going to add up and help reduce my overall cost of the leaps I got today. And as NVDA goes up in value over the next year, my long calls will also go up (hopefully). My plan for selling calls against the leaps is to collect enough premium on selling calls to cover the cost of the leaps. Imagine in February NVDA is at like $380 selling those $405 (or higher) calls is going to pay a lot more than $20 Then when it goes ITM, the real fun begins. So I plan on collecting a few bucks here and there the next few weeks, but then as each leap grows in value, I'll be able to pocket more. 4 3 Add Reaction

author: TradingTheTrend
text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. author: TradingTheTrend
text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. BTO = Buy To Open STC = Sell To Close STO = Sell To Open BTC = Buy To Close C = Call P = Put ITM = In The Money ATM = At The Money OTM = Outside The Money SL = Stop Loss PT = Price Target HOD = High of Day LOD = Low of Day ATH = All Time High ER = Earnings Report EOD = End of Day B/O = Breakout Pre / PM = Premarket AH = After Hours FOMO = Fear of Missing Out R/R = Risk Reward DD = Due Diligence PDT = Pattern Day Trader ETF = Exchange Traded Funds TA = Technical Analysis FA = Fundamental Analysis IPO = Initial Public Offering GTC = Good Til’ Canceled (order) GTD = Good Til’ Date (order) MM = Market Maker YOLO = You Only Live Once EMA = exponential moving average. RSI = relative strength index. VWAP = volume weighted average price. SS = short sell. Momo = momentum. Welcome to VIP Alerts ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 is option signals from our analysts. Read the format guide above before your first one. ⁠🛸spread-alerts is option spread signals from our analysts. ⁠🎰lotto-alerts is lottery ticket plays. Very high risk. These can go to zero. ⁠⚠stock-alerts-⚠ is where we alert our stock picks. ⁠💪member-alerts💪 Post your own trades or see what other members are trading. text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. author: TradingTheTrend
text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. BTO = Buy To Open STC = Sell To Close STO = Sell To Open BTC = Buy To Close C = Call P = Put ITM = In The Money ATM = At The Money OTM = Outside The Money SL = Stop Loss PT = Price Target HOD = High of Day LOD = Low of Day ATH = All Time High ER = Earnings Report EOD = End of Day B/O = Breakout Pre / PM = Premarket AH = After Hours FOMO = Fear of Missing Out R/R = Risk Reward DD = Due Diligence PDT = Pattern Day Trader ETF = Exchange Traded Funds TA = Technical Analysis FA = Fundamental Analysis IPO = Initial Public Offering GTC = Good Til’ Canceled (order) GTD = Good Til’ Date (order) MM = Market Maker YOLO = You Only Live Once EMA = exponential moving average. RSI = relative strength index. VWAP = volume weighted average price. SS = short sell. Momo = momentum. Welcome to VIP Alerts ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 is option signals from our analysts. Read the format guide above before your first one. ⁠🛸spread-alerts is option spread signals from our analysts. ⁠🎰lotto-alerts is lottery ticket plays. Very high risk. These can go to zero. ⁠⚠stock-alerts-⚠ is where we alert our stock picks. ⁠💪member-alerts💪 Post your own trades or see what other members are trading. These are member posts, not analyst calls. ⁠trade-log is an automatic log of every ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 position, open and closed, posted by @TradesTracker ⁠🔵options-watchlist is posted every morning before the open. author: TradingTheTrend
text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. BTO = Buy To Open STC = Sell To Close STO = Sell To Open BTC = Buy To Close C = Call P = Put ITM = In The Money ATM = At The Money OTM = Outside The Money SL = Stop Loss PT = Price Target HOD = High of Day LOD = Low of Day ATH = All Time High ER = Earnings Report EOD = End of Day B/O = Breakout Pre / PM = Premarket AH = After Hours FOMO = Fear of Missing Out R/R = Risk Reward DD = Due Diligence PDT = Pattern Day Trader ETF = Exchange Traded Funds TA = Technical Analysis FA = Fundamental Analysis IPO = Initial Public Offering GTC = Good Til’ Canceled (order) GTD = Good Til’ Date (order) MM = Market Maker YOLO = You Only Live Once EMA = exponential moving average. RSI = relative strength index. VWAP = volume weighted average price. SS = short sell. Momo = momentum. Welcome to VIP Alerts ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 is option signals from our analysts. Read the format guide above before your first one. ⁠🛸spread-alerts is option spread signals from our analysts. ⁠🎰lotto-alerts is lottery ticket plays. Very high risk. These can go to zero. ⁠⚠stock-alerts-⚠ is where we alert our stock picks. ⁠💪member-alerts💪 Post your own trades or see what other members are trading. These are member posts, not analyst calls. ⁠trade-log is an automatic log of every ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 position, open and closed, posted by @TradesTracker ⁠🔵options-watchlist is posted every morning before the open. Names we are watching and the triggers to watch. View the pinned message in ⁠🔵options-watchlist for more info. Trading School at the bottom of the server covers the fundamentals. Start here if you are newer to options. ⁠intro-to-options-trading ⁠the-greeks ⁠contracts ⁠candlesticks ⁠support-and-resistance ⁠hedging ⁠ema ⁠trendlines ⁠spreads-101 ⁠education tons of educational content. ⁠education-discussion have any trading questions? Feel free to ask here. Before your first trade Checkout ⁠meet-our-analysts to learn more about each of us. Read ⁠risk-management !!! Hope you enjoy! (edited) Monday, August 24, 2026 at 11:08 PM

text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. BTO = Buy To Open STC = Sell To Close STO = Sell To Open BTC = Buy To Close C = Call P = Put ITM = In The Money ATM = At The Money OTM = Outside The Money SL = Stop Loss PT = Price Target HOD = High of Day LOD = Low of Day ATH = All Time High ER = Earnings Report EOD = End of Day B/O = Breakout Pre / PM = Premarket AH = After Hours FOMO = Fear of Missing Out R/R = Risk Reward DD = Due Diligence PDT = Pattern Day Trader ETF = Exchange Traded Funds TA = Technical Analysis FA = Fundamental Analysis IPO = Initial Public Offering GTC = Good Til’ Canceled (order) GTD = Good Til’ Date (order) MM = Market Maker YOLO = You Only Live Once EMA = exponential moving average. RSI = relative strength index. VWAP = volume weighted average price. SS = short sell. Momo = momentum. Welcome to VIP Alerts ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 is option signals from our analysts. Read the format guide above before your first one. ⁠🛸spread-alerts is option spread signals from our analysts. ⁠🎰lotto-alerts is lottery ticket plays. Very high risk. author: TradingTheTrend
text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. BTO = Buy To Open STC = Sell To Close STO = Sell To Open BTC = Buy To Close C = Call P = Put ITM = In The Money ATM = At The Money OTM = Outside The Money SL = Stop Loss PT = Price Target HOD = High of Day LOD = Low of Day ATH = All Time High ER = Earnings Report EOD = End of Day B/O = Breakout Pre / PM = Premarket AH = After Hours FOMO = Fear of Missing Out R/R = Risk Reward DD = Due Diligence PDT = Pattern Day Trader ETF = Exchange Traded Funds TA = Technical Analysis FA = Fundamental Analysis IPO = Initial Public Offering GTC = Good Til’ Canceled (order) GTD = Good Til’ Date (order) MM = Market Maker YOLO = You Only Live Once EMA = exponential moving average. RSI = relative strength index. VWAP = volume weighted average price. SS = short sell. Momo = momentum. Welcome to VIP Alerts ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 is option signals from our analysts. Read the format guide above before your first one. ⁠🛸spread-alerts is option spread signals from our analysts. ⁠🎰lotto-alerts is lottery ticket plays. Very high risk. These can go to zero. ⁠⚠stock-alerts-⚠ is where we alert our stock picks. ⁠💪member-alerts💪 Post your own trades or see what other members are trading. These are member posts, not analyst calls. ⁠trade-log is an automatic log of every ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 position, open and closed, posted by @TradesTracker ⁠🔵options-watchlist is posted every morning before the open. Names we are watching and the triggers to watch. View the pinned message in ⁠🔵options-watchlist for more info. Trading School at the bottom of the server covers the fundamentals. Start here if you are newer to options. ⁠intro-to-options-trading ⁠the-greeks ⁠contracts ⁠candlesticks ⁠support-and-resistance ⁠hedging ⁠ema ⁠trendlines ⁠spreads-101 ⁠education tons of educational content. ⁠education-discussion have any trading questions? Feel free to ask here. Before your first trade Checkout ⁠meet-our-analysts to learn more about each of us. Read ⁠risk-management !!! Hope you enjoy! (edited) Monday, August 24, 2026 at 11:08 PM

text: TradingTheTrend — 10/25/20, 5:27 PM Sunday, October 25, 2020 at 5:27 PM Server Rules Do not share paid content outside this server. , No screenshots, forwards, copy-pastes, or relaying alerts to anyone outside TTT. One account per subscription. , Do not share logins or give a second person access to your account. Do not sign up with two different emails. Duplicate accounts get removed. text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. BTO = Buy To Open STC = Sell To Close STO = Sell To Open BTC = Buy To Close C = Call P = Put ITM = In The Money ATM = At The Money OTM = Outside The Money SL = Stop Loss PT = Price Target HOD = High of Day LOD = Low of Day ATH = All Time High ER = Earnings Report EOD = End of Day B/O = Breakout Pre / PM = Premarket AH = After Hours FOMO = Fear of Missing Out R/R = Risk Reward DD = Due Diligence PDT = Pattern Day Trader ETF = Exchange Traded Funds TA = Technical Analysis FA = Fundamental Analysis IPO = Initial Public Offering GTC = Good Til’ Canceled (order) GTD = Good Til’ Date (order) MM = Market Maker YOLO = You Only Live Once EMA = exponential moving average. text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. BTO = Buy To Open STC = Sell To Close STO = Sell To Open BTC = Buy To Close C = Call P = Put ITM = In The Money ATM = At The Money OTM = Outside The Money SL = Stop Loss PT = Price Target HOD = High of Day LOD = Low of Day ATH = All Time High ER = Earnings Report EOD = End of Day B/O = Breakout Pre / PM = Premarket AH = After Hours FOMO = Fear of Missing Out R/R = Risk Reward DD = Due Diligence PDT = Pattern Day Trader ETF = Exchange Traded Funds TA = Technical Analysis FA = Fundamental Analysis IPO = Initial Public Offering GTC = Good Til’ Canceled (order) GTD = Good Til’ Date (order) MM = Market Maker YOLO = You Only Live Once EMA = exponential moving average. RSI = relative strength index. VWAP = volume weighted average price. SS = short sell. Momo = momentum. Welcome to VIP Alerts ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 is option signals from our analysts. text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. BTO = Buy To Open STC = Sell To Close STO = Sell To Open BTC = Buy To Close C = Call P = Put ITM = In The Money ATM = At The Money OTM = Outside The Money SL = Stop Loss PT = Price Target HOD = High of Day LOD = Low of Day ATH = All Time High ER = Earnings Report EOD = End of Day B/O = Breakout Pre / PM = Premarket AH = After Hours FOMO = Fear of Missing Out R/R = Risk Reward DD = Due Diligence PDT = Pattern Day Trader ETF = Exchange Traded Funds TA = Technical Analysis FA = Fundamental Analysis IPO = Initial Public Offering GTC = Good Til’ Canceled (order) GTD = Good Til’ Date (order) MM = Market Maker YOLO = You Only Live Once EMA = exponential moving average. text: TradingTheTrend — 10/25/20, 5:27 PM Sunday, October 25, 2020 at 5:27 PM Server Rules Do not share paid content outside this server. , No screenshots, forwards, copy-pastes, or relaying alerts to anyone outside TTT. This includes group chats, other Discords, and social media. Sharing paid content is an immediate ban with no refund. One account per subscription. , Do not share logins or give a second person access to your account. Do not sign up with two different emails. Duplicate accounts get removed. We never DM you first. , If someone messages you offering signals, mentoring, account management, or a discount, it is a scammer impersonating us. Do not reply and do not send money. Report it in ⁠report-spam. No promoting or recruiting. , No other trading services, Discords, affiliate links, courses, or paid groups. No DMing members to sell them anything. This gets you banned without warning. Nothing here is financial advice. , Analysts share what they are doing and why. You decide what to take, how much to size, and when to exit. Every trade you place is yours. Read ⁠risk-management before your first one. Analysts cannot manage your account. , Do not ask an analyst what to do with a position you entered on your own, what size to trade, or whether to hold overnight. They do not know your account, your risk tolerance, or your situation, and answering would be irresponsible. Own your losses. , Everyone here takes losses, including the analysts. Do not blame the room, do not attack other members, and do not spiral in chat after a bad trade. If you are trading money you cannot lose, stop and reread ⁠risk-management. Keep it civil. , No harassment, slurs, personal attacks, or politics. Disagree about a setup all you want. Attack the idea, never the person. Stay on topic. , Post in the channel that fits. Alerts channels are for alerts, not commentary. Discord Terms of Service apply. , You must be 13+ to be here and 18+ to subscribe. Enforcement is warning, then mute, then removal. Rules 1, 2, and 4 skip straight to removal. Bans do not come with refunds. See ⁠terms-and-conditions. (edited) Sunday, August 2, 2026 at 11:12 PM

text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. author: TradingTheTrend
text: TradingTheTrend — 1/18/21, 1:16 AM Monday, January 18, 2021 at 1:16 AM How our alerts work Every alert uses the same format: ACTION TICKER STRIKE + TYPE EXPIRATION @ PRICE BTO = Buy To Open (this is the entry) STC = Sell To Close (this is the exit) c = call, p = put Example of a winner BTO AAPL 120c 11/06 @1.5 STC AAPL 120c 11/06 @3.0 for 100% gain Example of a loser BTO SNAP 40c 11/06 @1.00 STC SNAP 40c 11/06 @.90 for -10% We post both. Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. BTO = Buy To Open STC = Sell To Close STO = Sell To Open BTC = Buy To Close C = Call P = Put ITM = In The Money ATM = At The Money OTM = Outside The Money SL = Stop Loss PT = Price Target HOD = High of Day LOD = Low of Day ATH = All Time High ER = Earnings Report EOD = End of Day B/O = Breakout Pre / PM = Premarket AH = After Hours FOMO = Fear of Missing Out R/R = Risk Reward DD = Due Diligence PDT = Pattern Day Trader ETF = Exchange Traded Funds TA = Technical Analysis FA = Fundamental Analysis IPO = Initial Public Offering GTC = Good Til’ Canceled (order) GTD = Good Til’ Date (order) MM = Market Maker YOLO = You Only Live Once EMA = exponential moving average. RSI = relative strength index. VWAP = volume weighted average price. SS = short sell. Momo = momentum. Welcome to VIP Alerts ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 is option signals from our analysts. Read the format guide above before your first one. ⁠🛸spread-alerts is option spread signals from our analysts. ⁠🎰lotto-alerts is lottery ticket plays. Very high risk. These can go to zero. ⁠⚠stock-alerts-⚠ is where we alert our stock picks. ⁠💪member-alerts💪 Post your own trades or see what other members are trading. These are member posts, not analyst calls. ⁠trade-log is an automatic log of every ⁠🚨option-alerts🚨 position, open and closed, posted by @TradesTracker ⁠🔵options-watchlist is posted every morning before the open. Names we are watching and the triggers to watch. View the pinned message in ⁠🔵options-watchlist for more info. Trading School at the bottom of the server covers the fundamentals. Start here if you are newer to options. ⁠intro-to-options-trading ⁠the-greeks ⁠contracts ⁠candlesticks ⁠support-and-resistance ⁠hedging ⁠ema ⁠trendlines ⁠spreads-101 ⁠education tons of educational content. ⁠education-discussion have any trading questions? Feel free to ask here. Before your first trade Checkout ⁠meet-our-analysts to learn more about each of us. Read ⁠risk-management !!! Hope you enjoy! (edited) Monday, August 24, 2026 at 11:08 PM

Every trade goes in the log, win or lose. Things to know The price is per share, so @1.5 means $1.50 per share and $150 for one contract. Your fill will not always match the alert. Options move fast and spreads widen. If price has run well past the alerted entry, let it go and wait for the next one. Chasing is how members lose money on trades the room made money on. You size the position. The alert tells you what and where, never how much. text: jonntran APP — 8/31/26, 8:26 AM Monday, August 31, 2026 at 8:26 AM Observations: Overnight inventory for ES and NQ is net short, as volume has traded mostly below PDL. Focus and Scenarios: Net short inventory with the potential for a gap opening if prices cannot reclaim PDL and the last price. Both ES and NQ printed two-day overlapping value, so the two-day value will be the primary AOIs, along with recent MGI. With that said, they both have a multi-day value structure that could be the destination, using the context of the gap rules to assist. Primary Scenario: Gap Rules Go with the gap if sellers maintain acceptance below PDL. A reclaim of PDL and gap fill introduces the potential to traverse the two-day value. text: Option Sniper APP — 8/20/26, 4:24 PM Thursday, August 20, 2026 at 4:24 PM @Option Sniper (edited) Thursday, August 20, 2026 at 4:27 PM Option Sniper v1.14 is live — your prices now ride Schwab's streaming feed. Entries crawled, exits lagged, and a few of you got hurt. People running on Schwab's streaming feed never saw it. So now the app runs on that feed too. What changed: Streaming prices while you're in a trade. The moment you're in, Schwab pushes the bid to the app as it changes instead of the app asking once a second. Your stop and target react faster. The once-a-second check doesn't go away — it runs every five seconds as a truth check on the stream, and if the stream ever goes quiet or disagrees, the app drops straight back to full-speed polling on its own. You don't touch anything. A banner when Schwab is slow. If your broker's quote service bogs down, the app says so — with how far behind the quotes are — and clears it when things recover. It never blocks a button. A LIVE / POLL tag in the exit strip so you can see which feed is carrying your price at any moment. Both protect you; it's just telling you which. If you run your own program on Schwab's streaming connection: Schwab allows one per account and the app will not fight you for it. Flip off Use streaming prices in Settings and the app never touches it. As always, install it before the open or after the close. The installer has to close the app, and you don't want that happening while you're holding a position. 5 Add Reaction

text: Option Sniper APP — 8/6/26, 6:23 PM Thursday, August 6, 2026 at 6:23 PM Option Sniper v1.0.10 is live — grab it from the download page on the site: https://www.tradingdecoded.com/option-sniper This one leads with a bug fix, and it matters if you're on Webull. One of you sent a screenshot of an entry that came back ORDER REJECTED — 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS. The order wasn't rejected. It reached Webull fine. Option Sniper checks back a few times to see whether it filled, Webull rate-limited those status checks, and the app treated "I won't answer you right now" as "your order died." That's fixed. The app now waits out the limit and asks again, and it spaces the checks out so it's less likely to get throttled at all. And in the rare case it genuinely can't get an answer, it tells you the order was sent but unconfirmed and to check your broker — instead of telling you something false. If you ever see a rejection you don't trust, check your broker before re-firing. That habit is worth having regardless of what the app says. Thank you for the screenshot. That's exactly how this gets found. One more thing: Option Sniper will now tell you when there's a new version — a notice when you launch it, and a small arrow next to the version number that sticks around until you update. It never installs anything on its own, it just points you back here. You'll see it for the first time when the next release lands. When you do update, install it before the open or after the close. The installer has to close the app, and you don't want that happening while you're holding a position. (edited) Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 2:22 PM

text: Option Sniper APP — 8/19/26, 8:32 PM Wednesday, August 19, 2026 at 8:32 PM @Option Sniper Option Sniper v1.13 is live — and your Trade Tracker can now fill itself in. Grab it from the download page: https://www.tradingdecoded.com/option-sniper The headline: broker-verified trade syncing. Flip on Sync trades to Trade Tracker in the app's Settings and the app pulls your option trades straight from Schwab's own records and sends them to your Trade Tracker on the site. First run reaches back 60 days, and after that every trade shows up on its own — no CSV export, no manual entry. And because the numbers come from your broker instead of anybody's typing, they're the numbers. Paper trades sync too, tagged as paper so they never mix with your live record. Three honest details so nobody's surprised: — It syncs your Schwab option trades, not just trades placed through the app. The tracker becomes your real record, which is the point. — Webull live sync isn't built yet. Webull folks: your paper trades sync, but live trades still come in through the CSV upload for now. It's next on the list. — If your CSV history in the tracker goes back further than 60 days, the tracker will show you the exact date range to export from Schwab one last time to bridge the gap. After that you never touch a CSV again. The app also starts recording your account balance once a day, which is what draws your balance curve in the tracker going forward. That history starts the day you install this — one more reason not to sit on the update. Two fixes from your error reports: Updating no longer files a crash report on itself. Several of you "crashed" the second you updated to v1.12 — that was the installer closing the app, not a crash, and the app can tell the difference now. A one-second Schwab hiccup no longer sinks a fill check. During Schwab's bad morning on the 17th, an order could go through and then a single failed status check made the app give up confirming it and call the buy rejected while you were actually in the trade. It now rides through a bad answer and keeps checking. That one came straight out of the error reports — keep sending them. As always, install it before the open or after the close. The installer has to close the app, and you don't want that happening while you're holding a position. 5 Add Reaction

author: Option Sniper
text: Option Sniper APP — 8/16/26, 11:45 AM Sunday, August 16, 2026 at 11:45 AM @Option Sniper Option Sniper v1.12 is live — grab it from the download page on the site: https://www.tradingdecoded.com/option-sniper This one is mostly things that were wasting your time, found from the error reports you've been sending me. Keep sending them — every fix below came out of one. Webull people: if it would never connect, read this. A Webull API key created with 2FA turned on is rejected on every single request. Not just quotes — the very first call, the one that just asks Webull to list your accounts. So your key is correct, your account is funded, your app is approved, and it fails forever and tells you nothing useful. A couple of you have been fighting this for days. Generate the key with 2FA OFF and it works. The app now says so right where you paste the keys. The other Webull trap while I'm here: option quotes need OPRA Real-Time (Non-display) plus the free Nasdaq Basic, bought in the Open API Advanced Quotes tab on webullapp.com. A quote subscription you already pay Webull for in the app or the desktop terminal does not carry over to an API key. That one's Webull's rule, not mine, and it catches everybody. A close that filled will no longer tell you it was rejected. Two different bugs did this. One was the app racing itself — completing a close in the background and then reporting a rejection for an order that had already filled. The other was Schwab's edge dropping a connection mid-close, which the app treated as a dead end on the first try, leaving somebody sitting in a live position. It retries now — but carefully, and I want you to know exactly how carefully, because this is your money. It only re-sends when it can confirm the first order never reached Schwab and you're still holding the whole position. Blindly sending a second sell would leave you short, which is worse than the bug I'm fixing. If it can't be certain, it tells you to CHECK YOUR BROKER instead of guessing. That message means look, not panic. The ticker you pick stays picked. It used to quietly snap back to QQQ every time you reopened the app. At least one of you traded QQQ believing you were on SPY, twice. It was also a barely-lighter grey button among three grey buttons — the one you're on is now the biggest, brightest thing in the row. TRAIL is one tap. No more TRAIL → TRAIL? to confirm. I checked why the confirm was there before removing it; it was guarding nothing. And the app stopped claiming it lost the connection when it hadn't. One hiccup used to put that warning on screen for the rest of the session, even after everything was fine again. As always, install it before the open or after the close. The installer has to close the app, and you don't want that happening while you're holding a position. 4 2 1 Add Reaction

text: Option Sniper APP — 8/12/26, 2:20 PM Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 2:20 PM @Option Sniper Option Sniper v1.0.11 is live — grab it from the download page on the site: https://www.tradingdecoded.com/option-sniper Option Sniper runs on Mac now. That's the headline. It's a proper Mac build — signed and notarized by Apple, so it installs and opens like any other app instead of getting blocked. One limit worth knowing before you download: Apple Silicon only, meaning any Mac with an M1 through M4 chip. If you're on an older Intel Mac, this won't run and I'd rather tell you now than have you find out after the download. Mac users: connecting to Schwab uses the copy-and-paste step. That's expected on Mac, not something broken. The Windows installer is signed now too. Some of you hit a Windows screen calling Option Sniper an unrecognized app from an unknown publisher. One of you hit a stricter version of it that had no way through at all. That's what this fixes — the installer now carries a certificate naming Trading Decoded LLC. Being straight with you: you may still see "Windows protected your PC" for a while. Windows also weighs how many people have downloaded a file, and that takes time to build. The difference is that it now says who signed it. So make this your habit: Before you click Run anyway, check that it says Publisher: Trading Decoded LLC. If it doesn't say that, don't run it — you didn't get that file from me. Option Sniper now tells me when it breaks. One of you got into a trade, couldn't get out of it, and ended up closing it through Schwab's own screen. Something popped up in the app and it was gone before you could read it — so all I had was "something went wrong" and nothing to work from. That's on me to fix, and this is the fix. When the app hits an error now, it sends me what happened: the error itself, what the app believed about your trade at that moment, and a picture of the app window. That last one will show your balance and any open position, so I want you to know about it up front. It goes to me and nowhere else, and your broker tokens and license key are never in it. There's also a Report a problem button in the app now, under the day's trades. Use it when something feels wrong but the app never showed an error — that's the case I currently have no way of seeing. A sentence is plenty. If you'd rather it stayed off: Settings → Send error reports, one checkbox, and nothing leaves your machine. There's a button beside it to save a report to a folder if you'd rather email me the file yourself. This is temporary. Once the rough edges from the beta are gone, so is this. No trading logic changed in this release. Same watcher, same exits, same broker code. If 1.0.10 was behaving for you, this one behaves identically — it's the packaging that got fixed. As always, install it before the open or after the close. The installer has to close the app, and you don't want that happening while you're holding a position.

author: Option Sniper
text: Option Sniper APP — 8/6/26, 6:23 PM Thursday, August 6, 2026 at 6:23 PM Option Sniper v1.0.10 is live — grab it from the download page on the site: https://www.tradingdecoded.com/option-sniper This one leads with a bug fix, and it matters if you're on Webull. One of you sent a screenshot of an entry that came back ORDER REJECTED — 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS. The order wasn't rejected. It reached Webull fine. Option Sniper checks back a few times to see whether it filled, Webull rate-limited those status checks, and the app treated "I won't answer you right now" as "your order died." That's fixed. The app now waits out the limit and asks again, and it spaces the checks out so it's less likely to get throttled at all. And in the rare case it genuinely can't get an answer, it tells you the order was sent but unconfirmed and to check your broker — instead of telling you something false. If you ever see a rejection you don't trust, check your broker before re-firing. That habit is worth having regardless of what the app says. Thank you for the screenshot. That's exactly how this gets found. One more thing: Option Sniper will now tell you when there's a new version — a notice when you launch it, and a small arrow next to the version number that sticks around until you update. It never installs anything on its own, it just points you back here. You'll see it for the first time when the next release lands. When you do update, install it before the open or after the close. The installer has to close the app, and you don't want that happening while you're holding a position. (edited) Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 2:22 PM

author: Option Sniper
text: Option Sniper APP — Yesterday at 11:54 AM Wednesday, September 9, 2026 at 11:54 AM @Option Sniper Option Sniper v1.16 is live — a paper trade left open past expiration can't trap you anymore. Grab it from the download page: https://www.tradingdecoded.com/option-sniper Small release, and it exists because one of you lost a week to it. His app got killed by Windows about a minute after he entered a paper 0DTE. By the time he opened it back up, the contract had expired — and an expired contract has no price, so CLOSE just threw an error every time he clicked it. Worse, the app still thought it was holding something, so he couldn't reset his paper account, couldn't switch to live, couldn't do anything. Six days. What changed: The app settles an expired contract itself and hands you back a flat account. If you're sitting on a stuck paper position right now, update — it clears on the next launch. Crash reports finally say what happened. Five of you hit that same Windows-kills-the-app crash last week and every report came through saying nothing but "it didn't shut down cleanly." The detail that explains it was getting lost in the crash. It's written down first now. I still don't know the cause — but the next one will tell me. The price stream backs off properly. If Schwab kept dropping the connection, the app retried once a second forever. In one case that ran for days. Nothing changes about the prices you see. As always, install it before the open or after the close. The installer has to close the app, and you don't want that happening while you're holding a position.

text: Baba Neal — 10:34 AM Thursday, September 10, 2026 at 10:34 AM @everyone There’s a reason I’ve been super quiet with the plays. This price action has been whack-a-mole. A setup looks ready to go, then gets smacked right back down. That makes conviction harder to hold and options harder to manage, so I’m being selective while this chop plays out.I’m still watching for a potential upside expansion around the OpEx transition. As existing contracts expire and new positions come in, dealer hedging can shift. Vanna and charm can contribute to buying pressure under the right conditions, but that depends on positioning, changes in volatility, and how hedges adjust. OpEx itself doesn’t prevent the market from topping.My working thesis is that we could still see one more aggressive move higher, potentially the final squeeze that puts the nail in the coffin for trapped shorts. But price needs to confirm it. For now, my silence is intentional. I’m watching, preserving capital, and waiting for a move worth committing to.
